Jordan L14 February, 2019 at 10:39
Hey Ryan, what are your thoughts on this being called a 2018 release when it’s scheduled to come out the same day as 2019 Contenders Draft Picks, comes out over a month past the start of the new NFL year (March 13), 2 months after the Super Bowl, and really, in Q2 of 2019. Can any of these cards be considered a rookie card?
Ryan Cracknell14 February, 2019 at 10:51
@Jordan – All sports have pretty much moved to 12-month release calendars that extend past the end of the playing seasons. These will be Rookie Cards. As for Contenders, that can be seen as a college release, so a little different but I hear what you’re saying.

Jordan L14 February, 2019 at 10:39
Hey Ryan, what are your thoughts on this being called a 2018 release when it’s scheduled to come out the same day as 2019 Contenders Draft Picks, comes out over a month past the start of the new NFL year (March 13), 2 months after the Super Bowl, and really, in Q2 of 2019. Can any of these cards be considered a rookie card?
Ryan Cracknell14 February, 2019 at 10:51
@Jordan – All sports have pretty much moved to 12-month release calendars that extend past the end of the playing seasons. These will be Rookie Cards. As for Contenders, that can be seen as a college release, so a little different but I hear what you’re saying.

Will not purchase again.

RonNyc12 October, 2018 at 22:58
Very disappointing product. this year. Bought a 3-box case (as I did the previous 2 years) for over $1,500.00. Got nowhere near value for money. Half the on-card autos were smeared to some extent and got no big hits. Zero “Wow Factor.” This is essentially an inferior duplication of National Treasures and is, at this point, redundant. Will not purchase again.

IamNotARobot22 June, 2018 at 09:41
Is Panini using “Player worn” or “Game worn” memorabilia in this product too? The “player worn” memorabilia of established or legendary players is insulting and useless. It’s barely memorabilia – if a player puts the jersey on and immediately takes it off, it’s player worn. Big deal. Game worn is the way to go and would mean more to this collector. Panini is alienating me from collecting with stuff like this. I miss the days of several companies issuing cards.
Ryan Cracknell22 June, 2018 at 13:01
It likely varies from card to card. I’d suggest if you see something you’re interested in, ask to see the disclaimer on the back.

IamNotARobot22 June, 2018 at 09:41
Is Panini using “Player worn” or “Game worn” memorabilia in this product too? The “player worn” memorabilia of established or legendary players is insulting and useless. It’s barely memorabilia – if a player puts the jersey on and immediately takes it off, it’s player worn. Big deal. Game worn is the way to go and would mean more to this collector. Panini is alienating me from collecting with stuff like this. I miss the days of several companies issuing cards.
Ryan Cracknell22 June, 2018 at 13:01
It likely varies from card to card. I’d suggest if you see something you’re interested in, ask to see the disclaimer on the back.

IamNotARobot22 June, 2018 at 09:41
Is Panini using “Player worn” or “Game worn” memorabilia in this product too? The “player worn” memorabilia of established or legendary players is insulting and useless. It’s barely memorabilia – if a player puts the jersey on and immediately takes it off, it’s player worn. Big deal. Game worn is the way to go and would mean more to this collector. Panini is alienating me from collecting with stuff like this. I miss the days of several companies issuing cards.
Ryan Cracknell22 June, 2018 at 13:01
It likely varies from card to card. I’d suggest if you see something you’re interested in, ask to see the disclaimer on the back.
